Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the God of our fathers, and praised and glorified is Thy Name unto the ages. Amen. Let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, according as we have hoped in Thee. Blessed art Thou, O Lord; teach me Thy statutes. Blessed art Thou, O Master; make me to understand Thy statutes. Blessed art Thou, O Holy One; enlighten me with Thy statutes. Thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever; despise not the works of Thy hands. To Thee belongeth praise, to Thee belongeth song, to Thee belongeth glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

I believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Only-begotten, begotten of the Father before all ages; Light of Light, true God of true God, begotten, not made, of one essence with the Father, by Whom all things were made; Who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, and became man; and was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered, and was buried; and rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures; and ascended into heaven, and sitteth at the right hand of the Father; and shall come again with glory to judge the living and the dead, Whose kingdom shall have no end. And in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the Giver of life, Who proceedeth from the Father; Who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified; Who spake by the prophets. In one holy, catholic, and apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the remission of sins. I look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the age to come. Amen.

Here, if it is desired, the Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos appointed for the day may be read.

It is truly meet to bless thee, the Theotokos, ever-blessed and most blameless, and the Mother of our God. More honourable than the Cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the Seraphim; who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word, the very Theotokos, thee do we magnify.

Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us. (Thrice)

Glory, both now.

O Most Holy Trinity, have mercy on us. O Lord, cleanse us from our sins. O Master, pardon our iniquities. O Holy One, visit and heal our infirmities, for Thy Name's sake.

Lord, have mercy. (Thrice) Glory, both now.

Our Father, Who art in the heavens, hallowed be Thy Name. Thy Kingdom come. Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.

Through the prayers of our holy Fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for laying aside all defence, we sinners offer unto Thee, as Master, this supplication: have mercy on us.

Glory. O Lord, have mercy on us, for in Thee have we put our trust. Be not very angry with us, neither remember our iniquities; but look upon us now, as Thou art compassionate, and deliver us from our enemies; for Thou art our God, and we are Thy people; we are all the work of Thy hands, and we call upon Thy Name.

Both now. Open unto us the gate of compassion, O blessed Theotokos; for, hoping in thee, let us not perish; through thee may we be delivered from adversities, for thou art the salvation of the Christian race.

Lord, have mercy. (Forty times)

O Thou Who at all times and at every hour, both in heaven and on earth, art worshipped and glorified, O Christ God, Who art long-suffering, plenteous in mercy and compassion; Who lovest the just and showest mercy upon sinners; Who callest all to salvation through the promise of good things to come: Receive, O Lord, our prayers at this hour, and direct our lives toward Thy commandments. Sanctify our souls; make chaste our bodies; correct our thoughts; purify our intentions; and deliver us from every affliction, evil, and distress. Encompass us with Thy holy Angels, that, guarded and guided by their host, we may attain to the unity of the faith and to the knowledge of Thine unapproachable glory; for blessed art Thou unto the ages of ages. Amen.

Lord, have mercy. (Thrice) Glory, both now.

More honourable than the Cherubim, and beyond compare more glorious than the Seraphim; who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word, the very Theotokos, thee do we magnify.

In the Name of the Lord, father, bless.

Through the prayers of our holy Fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.

O Lord, Lord, Who hast delivered us from every arrow that flieth by day, deliver us also from every thing that walketh in darkness. Accept as an evening sacrifice the lifting up of our hands. Account us worthy also to pass through the course of the night unassailed by evil, and deliver us from every disturbance and fear that cometh of the devil. Grant unto our souls compunction, and to our thoughts carefulness concerning the trial at Thy dread and just judgment. Pierce our flesh with the fear of Thee, and mortify our members that are upon the earth; that, even in the stillness of sleep, we may be enlightened by the contemplation of Thy judgments. Take from us every unseemly fantasy and every harmful desire; and raise us up at the time of prayer, established in the faith, and advancing in Thy commandments; through the good pleasure and goodness of Thine Only-begotten Son, with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine all-holy and good and life-giving Spirit, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

O spotless, undefiled, incorrupt, most pure, chaste Virgin, Lady Theotokos, who by thy wondrous conceiving didst unite God the Word with men, and didst join the fallen nature of our race to heavenly things; thou only hope of the hopeless, and helper of the assailed, ready protection of them that flee unto thee, and refuge of all Christians: turn not away from me, a sinner, defiled, who with shameful thoughts and words and deeds have made myself wholly unprofitable, and through slothfulness of mind have become a slave to the pleasures of life. But as the Mother of the God Who loveth mankind, with love for mankind have compassion upon me a sinner and a prodigal, and accept my prayer, which is offered to thee out of defiled lips; and making use of thy boldness as a Mother, entreat thy Son and our Master and Lord that He may open unto me also the compassionate loving-kindness of His goodness; and that, overlooking my numberless transgressions, He may turn me to repentance, and show me forth as a tried doer of His commandments. And be thou ever near me as merciful, compassionate, and loving; in this present life a fervent protectress and helper, repelling the assaults of adversaries and guiding me to salvation; and at the time of my departure caring for my wretched soul, and driving far from it the dark countenances of the evil demons; and in the dreadful day of judgment delivering me from eternal torment, and showing me forth an inheritor of the ineffable glory of thy Son and our God. May I attain unto this, O my Lady, most holy Theotokos, through thy mediation and assistance; through the grace and love toward mankind of thine Only-begotten Son, our Lord and God and Saviour Jesus Christ. To Whom is due all glory, honour, and worship, together with His unoriginate Father, and His all-holy and good and life-giving Spirit, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

And grant unto us, O Master, as we go to our sleep, rest of body and soul; and preserve us from the gloomy slumber of sin, and from every dark pleasure of the night. Calm the impulses of the passions; quench the fiery darts of the evil one that are craftily directed against us; suppress the rebellions of our flesh, and lull to sleep all our earthly and material thoughts. And grant unto us, O God, a watchful mind, a chaste understanding, a sober heart, and a sleep light and free from every fantasy of the devil. Raise us up at the time of prayer, strengthened in Thy commandments, and holding steadfastly within us the remembrance of Thy judgments. Grant us to speak of Thy glory all the night long, that we may praise and bless and glorify Thine all-honourable and majestic Name, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

O most glorious Ever-Virgin Mary, Mother of Christ God, present our prayer to thy Son and our God, that through thee He may save our souls.

My hope is the Father, my refuge is the Son, my protection is the Holy Spirit: O Holy Trinity, glory to Thee.

Glory to Thee, O Christ God, our hope, glory to Thee. Glory, both now. Lord, have mercy. (Thrice) Father, bless.

May Christ our true God, through the prayers of His most pure Mother, of the holy and God-bearing Fathers, and of all the Saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loveth mankind. Amen.
prayers.note: Prayed before sleep, at the close of the day. On the eves of feasts the troparion and kontakion of the feast may be added; a canon to the Theotokos may also be read where marked.
prayers.src: Reader's service. Psalms from the King James Version (public domain); psalm numbers follow the Septuagint, as used in the services.

prayers.title: It Is Truly Meet
prayers.body: It is truly meet to bless you, O Theotokos, ever-blessed and most pure, and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the Cherubim, and more glorious beyond compare than the Seraphim: without defilement you gave birth to God the Word. True Theotokos, we magnify you.
prayers.src: Orthodox Daily Prayers, St. Tikhon's Seminary Press (public domain)

prayers.title: O Virgin Theotokos, Rejoice
prayers.body: Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos! Mary, full of Grace, the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb, for you have borne the Savior of our souls.
prayers.src: Orthodox Daily Prayers, St. Tikhon's Seminary Press (public domain)

prayers.title: Prayer to the Most Holy Theotokos
prayers.body:
O undefiled, immaculate, incorrupt, and most pure Lady, the pure Virgin Bride of God: through your most glorious birth-giving, you united God the Word to mankind, and joined our fallen human nature to the heavenly. You are the only hope of the hopeless, the aid of the embattled, a ready help to those who run to you, and a refuge for all Christians. Do not turn away from me, who am sinful and vile, who have made myself useless through defiled thoughts, words, and deeds. As Mother of the God Who loves mankind, have pity on me, a prodigal sinner, in that same love for mankind. Receive the prayer I offer to you with defiled lips, and pray to your Son, our Master and Lord, with your maternal boldness, that He may open even to me the goodness of His deep love for mankind. May He overlook my countless transgressions, turn me to repentance, and make me an experienced keeper of His commandments.

Stand by me always in your mercy, compassion, and love of good. Be my fervent intercessor and help in this life, driving off the assaults of enemies and guiding me to salvation. Guard my wretched soul at the time of my death, driving away the dark forms of the evil demons. Deliver me from eternal torment at the Day of Judgment, and reveal me an heir of the inexpressible glory of your Son and our God. May I receive this, my Lady most glorious Theotokos, through your help and intercession, through the Grace and love for mankind of your only-begotten Son, our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ, to Whom belong all glory, honor, and worship, with His unoriginate Father and His most holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Orthodox Daily Prayers (public domain); a prayer of the Monk Paul of the Evergetis monastery

prayers.title: The Small Paraklesis
prayers.body:
To the Theotokos let us run now most fervently, we sinners all and wretched ones, and fall prostrate, in repentance crying from the depths of our souls: O Lady, come to our aid, have compassion upon us; hasten, for we perish from our many transgressions; turn not your servants away with empty hands, for you alone are our hope.

Most Holy Theotokos, save us.

By the many temptations am I held; seeking to be saved, to you I have recourse. O Mother of the Word and Virgin, deliver me from all hardship and distress.

Most Holy Theotokos, save us.

The assaults of the passions trouble me, and fill my soul with great despondency. Still them, O Maiden, with the calm of your Son and your God, O All-Undefiled One.

Most Holy Theotokos, save us.

I hold you as the Protection and the Intercessor of my life, O Virgin who gave birth to God. Pilot me to your haven, O Cause of good things, O Support of the faithful, O only all-hymned one.

Most Holy Theotokos, save us.

I pray you, O Virgin, dispel the storm of my sorrows and my spiritual turmoil; for you, O Bride of God, gave birth to Christ, the Origin of stillness, O only most pure one.

Most Holy Theotokos, save us.

Deliver us from harm, O pure Theotokos who gave birth to the Eternal Redemption, and the Peace which surpasses all understanding.

Most Holy Theotokos, save us.

I know you as the Intercessor of my life and a firm rampart, O Virgin; you scatter the assaults of temptations and drive off the onsets of the demons; and I pray to you always: deliver me from the corruption of my passions.

Most Holy Theotokos, save us.

Be a haven for me, and the protection of my life, O Virgin, and a help, an unshakable wall, a refuge and shelter, and a rejoicing, for those who flee to you.

O Champion Leader and Protectress of Christians, the unfailing advocate before the Creator: despise not the cry of us sinners, but in your goodness come speedily to help us who call upon you in faith. Hasten to hear our petition, and to make supplication for us, O Theotokos, for you ever protect those who honor you.

It is truly meet to bless you, O Theotokos, ever-blessed and most pure, and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the Cherubim, and more glorious beyond compare than the Seraphim: without defilement you gave birth to God the Word. True Theotokos, we magnify you.

Higher than the heavens above are you, and purer far than the radiance of the sun, you who have redeemed us from the curse that held us bound, O Mistress of all creation: with hymns let us honor you.

From the great multitude of my transgressions, ill am I in body, and ailing too in soul. To you do I flee, the one full of grace; O hope of the hopeless, do you come to my aid.

O Lady and Mother of Him who saves, receive the supplications of us your unworthy servants, and intercede with Him Whom you brought forth: O Mistress of the world, be our mediation.

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us; for laying aside all defense, we sinners offer unto Thee, as Master, this supplication: have mercy on us.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. O Lord, have mercy on us, for in Thee have we put our trust; be not exceedingly angry with us, nor remember our iniquities, but look down upon us even now in Thy compassion, and deliver us from our enemies; for Thou art our God, and we are Thy people; we are all the work of Thy hands, and we have called upon Thy name.

Both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen. Open unto us the door of thy compassion, O blessed Theotokos; hoping in thee, may we not perish, but through thee may we be delivered from adversities, for thou art the salvation of the Christian people.
prayers.note: The principal hymns of the Small Supplicatory Canon to the Theotokos (Paraklesis), composed by the monk Theosterictos. The full service is sung with Psalms 142 and 50, the Canon in its odes, the Gospel, and the petitions; the order above gives the troparia, Kontakion, and megalynaria most often prayed.
prayers.src: Orthodox Daily Prayers, St. Tikhon's Seminary Press (public domain); the Supplicatory Canon to the Theotokos

prayers.title: To the Guardian Angel (Morning)
prayers.body:
O Holy Angel, who stand by my wretched soul and my passionate life: do not abandon me, a sinner, neither depart from me because of my lack of self-control. Leave no room for the evil demon to gain control of me through the violence of this mortal body. Strengthen my weak and feeble hand, and instruct me in the path of salvation.

O holy Angel of God, the guardian and protector of my wretched soul and body: forgive all the sorrows I have caused you, every day of my life. If I have sinned in this past night, protect me during this day. Keep me from every adverse temptation, that I may not anger God by any sin. Pray to the Lord for me, that He may establish me in His fear, and make me, His servant, worthy of His goodness. Amen.
prayers.src: Orthodox Daily Prayers, St. Tikhon's Seminary Press (public domain)

prayers.title: To the Guardian Angel (Before Sleep)
prayers.body: Angel of Christ, my holy guardian, the protector of my soul and body: forgive me for all the sins I have committed this day. Deliver me from all the evil of my militant Enemy, that I may not anger my God by any sin. Pray for me, your sinful and unworthy servant, that you may show me worthy of the goodness and mercy of the All-Holy Trinity, and the Mother of my Lord Jesus Christ, and all the saints. Amen.
prayers.src: Orthodox Daily Prayers, St. Tikhon's Seminary Press (public domain)

prayers.title: Prayer of St. Basil the Great
prayers.body:
O Sovereign Lord Jesus Christ our God, source of life and immortality, Author of all creation visible and invisible, the co-eternal and co-everlasting Son of the eternal Father, Who through the abundance of Thy goodness didst in these last days put on flesh, and wast crucified and buried for us ungrateful and graceless ones, and by Thine own Blood didst renew our nature corrupted by sin: do Thou Thyself, O immortal King, receive the repentance of me a sinner; incline Thine ear unto me, and hearken to my words. For I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned against heaven and before Thee, and I am not worthy to look upon the height of Thy glory; for I have provoked Thy goodness, having transgressed Thy commandments and not obeyed Thy ordinances.

But Thou, O Lord, being long-suffering, forbearing, and of great mercy, hast not given me up to perish in mine iniquities, but ever awaitest my conversion. For Thou, O Lover of mankind, hast said through Thy prophet: I desire not the death of the sinner, but that he should turn from his way and live. For Thou wiliest not, O Master, to destroy the work of Thy hands, neither hast Thou pleasure in the destruction of men, but desirest that all should be saved and come to the knowledge of the truth.

Wherefore I also, though I am unworthy of heaven and of earth and of this passing life, having subjected myself wholly to sin and become the slave of pleasures and defaced Thine image, yet being Thy work and Thy creature, despair not of mine own salvation, wretch that I am, but taking courage in Thine immeasurable compassion, I draw near. Receive me, therefore, O Christ, Lover of mankind, as Thou didst receive the harlot, the thief, the publican, and the prodigal; and take away the heavy burden of my sins, Thou Who takest away the sin of the world and healest the infirmities of men, Who callest unto Thyself them that are weary and heavy laden and givest them rest; for Thou camest not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

And cleanse me from all defilement of flesh and spirit, and teach me to perfect holiness in Thy fear; that with the clear witness of my conscience, receiving the portion of Thy Holy Things, I may be united to Thy holy Body and Blood, and may have Thee dwelling and abiding in me with the Father and Thy Holy Spirit. Yea, O Lord Jesus Christ my God, let not the communion of Thy most pure and life-giving Mysteries be unto me for judgment, nor let me through partaking thereof unworthily become sick in soul and body; but grant me, until my last breath, to receive without condemnation the portion of Thy Holy Things, unto the communion of the Holy Spirit, as a provision for life eternal, and as an acceptable defense before Thy dread judgment seat; that I also, with all Thine elect, may become a partaker of Thine incorruptible blessings which Thou hast prepared for them that love Thee, O Lord, in whom Thou art glorified unto the ages. Amen.
prayers.note: This is among the first of the prayers said on the morning of Communion. The full rule of preparation also includes the Canon of Repentance to our Lord Jesus Christ, the Supplicatory Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos, and the Canon to the Guardian Angel, read the evening before, together with the appointed fast and, as your spiritual father directs, confession. Keep the measure your spiritual father gives.
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: First Prayer of St. John Chrysostom
prayers.body:
O Lord my God, I know that I am not worthy nor sufficient that Thou shouldst enter under the roof of the house of my soul, for all is desolate and fallen in ruin, and Thou hast not in me a place worthy to lay Thy head. But as from the highest heaven Thou didst humble Thyself for our sake, so now conform Thyself to my lowliness. And as Thou didst consent to lie in a cave and in a manger of dumb beasts, so consent also to lie in the manger of my unspiritual soul, and to enter my defiled body.

And as Thou didst not disdain to enter and to sup with sinners in the house of Simon the leper, so consent also to enter the house of my humble soul, leprous and sinful. And as Thou didst not reject the woman who was a harlot and a sinner, like me, when she drew near and touched Thee, so be compassionate also with me a sinner, as I draw near and touch Thee. And as Thou didst not abhor her foul and unclean mouth when she kissed Thy most pure feet, so abhor not me, O my Lord and God, but vouchsafe unto me the communion of Thy most holy Body and Blood, unto the sanctification, enlightenment, and strengthening of my soul and body, unto the relief of the burden of my many sins, unto preservation from every diabolical practice, unto the mortification of the passions, unto the keeping of Thy commandments, unto the increase of Thy divine grace, and unto the attainment of Thy Kingdom.

For not in contempt do I draw near unto Thee, O Christ my God, but taking courage in Thine unspeakable goodness, and lest by long abstaining from Thy communion I become a prey to the noetic wolf. Wherefore I pray Thee, O Master, Who alone art holy: sanctify my soul and body, my mind and heart, my reins and inward parts; renew me wholly, and root Thy fear in my members, and make Thy sanctification indelible within me. Be Thou my helper and defender, guiding my life in peace, and vouchsafing me to stand at the right hand of Thy chosen ones; through the prayers and supplications of Thy most pure Mother, of Thine immaterial ministers and most pure powers, and of all the saints who from the ages have been well-pleasing unto Thee. Amen.
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: Prayer of St. John of Damascus
prayers.body: O Sovereign Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who alone hast authority to forgive men their sins: overlook in Thy goodness and love for mankind all mine offenses, whether committed with knowledge or in ignorance, and make me worthy to receive without condemnation Thy divine, glorious, most pure, and life-giving Mysteries; not unto punishment, nor unto an increase of sins, but unto purification and sanctification, and as a pledge of the life and Kingdom to come, as a protection and a help, and unto the overthrow of mine adversaries, and unto the blotting out of my many transgressions. For Thou art a God of mercy and compassion and love for mankind, and unto Thee we ascribe glory, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.note: The attribution of this prayer differs between traditions, and it is given here as received, without judgment between them. The Greek Horologion ascribes it to St. John Chrysostom (4th century); the Slavonic Molitvoslov and the English prayer-book tradition ascribe it to St. John of Damascus (8th century).
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: Prayer of St. Basil the Great Before Receiving
prayers.body: I know, O Lord, that I partake unworthily of Thine immaculate Body and Thy precious Blood, and that I am guilty, and eat and drink condemnation to myself, not discerning the Body and Blood of Thee my Christ and God; but taking courage in Thy compassion, I draw near unto Thee Who hast said: He that eateth My Flesh and drinketh My Blood abideth in Me, and I in him. Have compassion, therefore, O Lord, and make not an example of me, a sinner, but deal with me according to Thy mercy; and let these Holy Things be unto me for healing, and purification, and enlightenment, and preservation, and salvation, and unto the sanctification of soul and body; unto the driving away of every phantasy and evil practice and activity of the devil working mentally in my members; unto boldness and love toward Thee; unto the correction and grounding of my life; unto the increase of virtue and perfection; unto the fulfilling of Thy commandments; unto the communion of the Holy Spirit, as a provision for life eternal, and as an acceptable defense before Thy dread judgment seat; not unto judgment, nor unto condemnation. Amen.
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: Prayer of St. Symeon Metaphrastes
prayers.body: O only pure and sinless Lord, Who through the ineffable compassion of Thy love for mankind didst assume our whole nature through the pure and virgin blood of her who supernaturally conceived Thee by the coming of the Divine Spirit and by the will of the Eternal Father; O Christ Jesus, Wisdom and Peace and Power of God, Who in Thine assumption of our nature didst suffer Thy life-giving and saving Passion, the Cross, the Nails, the Spear, and Death: mortify all the deadly passions of my body. Thou Who in Thy burial didst spoil the dominions of hell, bury with good thoughts my evil schemes and scatter the spirits of wickedness. Thou Who by Thy life-giving Resurrection on the third day didst raise up our fallen forefather, raise me up who am sunk in sin, and set before me ways of repentance. Thou Who by Thy glorious Ascension didst deify our nature which Thou hadst assumed, and didst honor it by Thy session at the right hand of the Father, make me worthy, by the partaking of Thy holy Mysteries, of a place at Thy right hand among those who are saved. Thou Who by the descent of the Spirit, the Paraclete, didst make Thy holy Disciples worthy vessels, make me also a recipient of His coming. Thou Who art to come again to judge the world with justice, grant me also to meet Thee on the clouds, my Maker and Creator, with all Thy saints; that I may unendingly glorify and praise Thee, with Thine eternal Father and Thine all-holy and good and life-giving Spirit, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: Prayer of St. Symeon the New Theologian
prayers.body:
From sullied lips, from an abominable heart, from an unclean tongue, out of a polluted soul, receive my prayer, O my Christ. Reject me not, nor my words, nor my ways, nor even my shamelessness, but give me courage to say what I desire, O my Christ; and even more, teach me what to do and to say.

I have sinned more than the harlot who, on learning where Thou wast lodging, bought myrrh and dared to come and anoint Thy feet, my Christ, my Lord and my God. As Thou didst not repulse her when she drew near from her heart, neither, O Word, abominate me; but grant me Thy feet to clasp and to kiss, and with a flood of tears, as with most precious myrrh, dare to anoint them. Wash me with my tears, and purify me with them, O Word; forgive my sins, and grant me pardon.

Thou knowest the multitude of my evil deeds, Thou knowest also my wounds, and Thou seest my bruises; but also Thou knowest my faith, and Thou beholdest my willingness, and Thou hearest my sighs. Nothing escapeth Thee, my God, my Maker, my Redeemer, not even a tear-drop, nor part of a drop. Thine eyes know what I have not yet achieved, and in Thy book things not yet done are written by Thee. See my lowliness, see how great is my toil, and take from me all my sins, O God of all; that with a clean heart, a trembling mind, and a contrite spirit I may partake of Thy pure and all-holy Mysteries, by which all who eat and drink Thee with sincerity of heart are quickened and deified.

For Thou, my Lord, hast said: Whoever eateth My Flesh and drinketh My Blood abideth in Me, and I in him. Wholly true is the word of my Lord and God; for whoever partaketh of Thy divine and deifying Gifts is certainly not alone, but is with Thee, my Christ, Light of the Triune Sun which illumineth the world. And that I may not remain alone without Thee, the Giver of Life, my Breath, my Life, my Joy, the salvation of the world, therefore have I drawn near to Thee, as Thou seest, with tears and with a contrite spirit.

I beseech Thee, O Ransom of mine offences, to receive me; and that I may partake without condemnation of Thy life-giving and perfect Mysteries, that Thou mayest remain, as Thou hast said, with me, thrice-wretched as I am; lest the tempter find me without Thy grace, and craftily seize me, and having deceived me, seduce me from Thy deifying words. Therefore I fall at Thy feet, and fervently cry to Thee: as Thou didst receive the Prodigal and the Harlot who drew near to Thee, so have compassion and receive me, the profligate and the prodigal, as with a contrite spirit I now draw near to Thee.

I know, O Saviour, that no other hath sinned against Thee as I, nor hath done the deeds that I have committed. But this again I know, that not the greatness of mine offences nor the multitude of my sins surpasseth the great patience of my God and His extreme love for mankind; but with the oil of compassion Thou dost purify and enlighten those who fervently repent, and dost make them children of the light and sharers of Thy divine nature; and Thou actest most generously, for what is strange to angels and to the minds of men Thou often tellest unto them, as unto Thy true friends.

These things make me bold, my Christ; these things give me wings; and I take courage from the wealth of Thy goodness toward us. And rejoicing and trembling at once, I who am straw partake of Fire, and, strange wonder! I am ineffably bedewed, like the bush of old which burnt and yet was not consumed. Therefore with thankful mind, and with thankful heart, and with thankfulness in all the members of my soul and body, I worship and magnify and glorify Thee, my God, for Thou art blessed, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: Second Prayer of St. John Chrysostom
prayers.body: I am not worthy, O Lord and Master, that Thou shouldst enter under the roof of my soul; but since Thou in Thy love for mankind dost will to dwell in me, I take courage and approach. Thou commandest: I will open wide the doors, which Thou alone didst create, that Thou mayest enter with Thy wonted love for mankind, enter and enlighten my darkened thought. I believe that Thou wilt do this; for Thou didst not banish the Harlot who came to Thee with tears, nor reject the Publican who repented, nor drive away the Thief who acknowledged Thy Kingdom, nor abandon the repentant persecutor to himself; but all who came to Thee in repentance Thou didst number in the company of Thy friends, O Thou Who alone art blessed always, now and unto endless ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: Third Prayer of St. John Chrysostom
prayers.body: O Lord Jesus Christ my God, remit, forgive, absolve, and pardon the sins, offences, and transgressions which I, Thy sinful, useless, and unworthy servant, have committed from my youth up to the present day and hour, whether with knowledge or in ignorance, whether by words or deeds or intentions or thoughts, and whether by habit or through any of my senses. And through the intercessions of her who conceived Thee without seed, the immaculate and ever-virgin Mary Thy Mother, my only sure hope and protection and salvation, make me worthy to receive without condemnation Thy pure, immortal, life-giving, and dread Mysteries, unto the forgiveness of sins and unto life everlasting; unto sanctification and enlightenment and strength and healing and health of soul and body; and unto the blotting out and complete destruction of mine evil reasonings and intentions and prejudices, and of the nocturnal fantasies of dark and evil spirits. For Thine is the kingdom and the power and the glory and the honor and the worship, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: Second Prayer of St. John of Damascus
prayers.body: I stand before the doors of Thy sanctuary, and yet I do not put away my terrible thoughts. But do Thou, O Christ our God, Who didst justify the Publican, and hadst mercy on the Canaanite woman, and didst open the gates of Paradise to the Thief, open unto me the depths of Thy love for mankind; and as I approach and touch Thee, receive me as Thou didst receive the Harlot and the woman with the issue of blood; for the one, by touching the hem of Thy garment, easily received healing, and the other, by clasping Thy most pure feet, obtained release from her sins. And I, in my pitiableness, dare to receive Thy whole Body: let me not be burnt, but receive me as Thou didst receive them; enlighten the senses of my soul, and consume the stains of my sins; through the intercessions of her who bore Thee without seed, and of the heavenly Powers; for Thou art blessed unto the ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: I Believe, O Lord, and I Confess
prayers.body: I believe, O Lord, and I confess that Thou art truly the Christ, the Son of the living God, Who camest into the world to save sinners, of whom I am first. I believe also that this is truly Thine own most pure Body, and that this is truly Thine own most precious Blood. Therefore I pray Thee: have mercy upon me, and forgive me my transgressions, both voluntary and involuntary, of word and of deed, of knowledge and of ignorance; and make me worthy to partake without condemnation of Thy most pure Mysteries, for the remission of sins, and unto life everlasting. Amen.
prayers.note: The confession of faith said by all before receiving Holy Communion.
prayers.src: The Divine Liturgy (received text)

prayers.title: Before Communion: Verses of St. Symeon Metaphrastes
prayers.body:
Behold, I approach for Divine Communion. O Creator, burn me not as I partake; for Thou art Fire which consumeth the unworthy. But cleanse me from every defilement.

Tremble, O man, beholding the deifying Blood; for it is a coal that burneth the unworthy. The Body of God both deifieth and nourisheth me: it deifieth the spirit and wondrously nourisheth the mind.

Thou hast ravished me with longing, O Christ, and by Thy divine love Thou hast transformed me; but burn away my sins with spiritual fire, and count me worthy to be filled with delight in Thee, that, leaping for joy, O gracious Lord, I may magnify Thy two comings. Amen.
prayers.src: Received text of the Order of Preparation for Holy Communion; public-domain English per Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic Church (1906)

prayers.title: Of Thy Mystical Supper
prayers.body:
Of Thy Mystical Supper, O Son of God, accept me today as a communicant; for I will not speak of Thy Mystery to Thine enemies, neither like Judas will I give Thee a kiss; but like the thief will I confess Thee: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom.

Not unto judgment nor unto condemnation be my partaking of Thy Holy Mysteries, O Lord, but unto the healing of soul and body. Amen.
prayers.note: The communion hymn sung as the faithful approach the Chalice.
prayers.src: The Divine Liturgy (received text)

prayers.title: Thanksgiving After Communion
prayers.body: I thank Thee, O Lord my God, that Thou hast not rejected me, a sinner, but hast made me worthy to be a partaker of Thy Holy Mysteries. I thank Thee that Thou hast granted me, the unworthy, to partake of Thy most pure and heavenly Gifts. But, O Master Who lovest mankind, Who for our sake didst die and rise again, and didst bestow upon us these Thy dread and life-giving Mysteries for the wellbeing and sanctification of our souls and bodies: grant that these may be unto me for the healing of soul and body, for the averting of every adversary, for the enlightenment of the eyes of my heart, for the peace of my soul's powers, for faith unashamed, for love unfeigned, for the keeping of Thy commandments, for an increase of Thy divine grace, and for the attainment of Thy Kingdom; that being kept by them in Thy holiness, I may ever remember Thy grace, and no longer live for myself, but for Thee, our Master and Benefactor. And so, when I have departed this life in the hope of life eternal, may I attain unto everlasting rest, where the sound of those that keep festival is unceasing, and the gladness is endless of those that behold the ineffable beauty of Thy countenance. For Thou art the true desire and the unspeakable joy of those that love Thee, O Christ our God, and all creation doth hymn Thee unto the ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Prayers of Thanksgiving after Holy Communion (received text)

prayers.title: Thanksgiving of St. Basil the Great
prayers.body:
O Master, Christ God, King of the ages and Maker of all things, I thank Thee for all the good things which Thou hast bestowed upon me, and for the communion of Thy most pure and life-giving Mysteries. I pray Thee, therefore, O Good One and Lover of mankind: keep me under Thy protection and in the shadow of Thy wings; and grant me, even to my last breath, to partake worthily, with a pure conscience, of Thy holy things, unto the remission of sins and unto life everlasting. For Thou art the Bread of life, the Source of holiness, the Giver of good things, and unto Thee we ascribe glory, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace, according to Thy word; for mine eyes have seen Thy salvation, which Thou hast prepared before the face of all people: a light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of Thy people Israel.
prayers.src: Prayers of Thanksgiving after Holy Communion (received text); concluding with Luke 2:29-32

prayers.title: For Finding a Spiritual Father
prayers.body: O Lord, Who desirest not the death of a sinner, but that he should turn and live, Thou Who didst come down to earth in order to restore life to those lying dead through sin, and to make them worthy of seeing Thee, the true Light, so far as that is possible to man: send me a man who knoweth Thee, that, in serving him and subjecting myself to him with all my strength, as unto Thee, and in doing Thy will in his, I may please Thee, the only true God; and that even I, a sinner, may be made worthy of Thy Kingdom. Amen.
prayers.note: A prayer for one who seeks a spiritual father. Seek such a guide through your parish and bishop; until one is found, be guided by your parish priest, by the Holy Scriptures, and by the writings of the Fathers.
prayers.src: St. Symeon the New Theologian, Catechetical Discourses (Sources Chretiennes 129, pp. 186-188); cited in Hierotheos of Nafpaktos, Orthodox Psychotherapy, and Kallistos Ware, The Spiritual Father in Orthodox Christianity

prayers.title: In Time of Trouble
prayers.body: O God, our help and assistance, Who art just and merciful, and Who hearest the supplications of Thy people: look down upon me, a miserable sinner, have mercy upon me, and deliver me from this trouble that besets me. I acknowledge and believe, O Lord, that all trials of this life are given by Thee for our chastisement when we drift away from Thee and disobey Thy commandments. Deal not with me after my sins, but according to Thy bountiful mercies, for I am the work of Thy hands, and Thou knowest my weakness. Grant me, I beseech Thee, Thy divine helping grace, and endow me with patience and strength to endure my tribulations with complete submission to Thy will. Thou knowest my misery and suffering, and to Thee, my only hope and refuge, I flee for relief and comfort; trusting in Thine infinite love and compassion, that in due time, when Thou knowest best, Thou wilt deliver me from this trouble, and turn my distress into comfort; and I shall rejoice in Thy mercy, and exalt and praise Thy holy Name, O Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Prayer in time of trouble, received in the Antiochian Orthodox prayer-book tradition

prayers.title: For Healing in Sickness
prayers.body: O Lord Jesus Christ, our Savior, Physician of souls and bodies, Who didst become man and suffer death on the Cross for our salvation, and through Thy tender love and compassion didst heal all manner of sickness and affliction: do Thou, O Lord, visit me in my suffering, and grant me grace and strength to bear this sickness with which I am afflicted, with Christian patience and submission to Thy will, trusting in Thy loving-kindness and tender mercy. Bless, I pray Thee, the means used for my recovery, and those who administer them. Look upon my weakness, and deal not with me after my sins, but according to the multitude of Thy mercies. Grant that my sickness may be the means of my true repentance and amendment of life according to Thy will, that I may spend the rest of my days in Thy love and fear; that my soul, being helped by Thy grace and sanctified by Thy Holy Mysteries, may be prepared for its passage to eternal life, and there, in the company of Thy blessed Saints, may praise and glorify Thee, with Thy eternal Father and life-giving Spirit. Amen.
prayers.src: Prayer for the sick, Antiochian Orthodox prayer-book tradition; cf. the Book of Needs (Trebnik)

prayers.title: Before a Journey
prayers.body: O Lord Jesus Christ our God, the true and living way: be Thou, O Master, my companion, guide, and guardian during my journey; deliver and protect me from all danger, misfortune, and temptation; that, being so defended by Thy divine power, I may have a peaceful and successful journey, and arrive safely at my destination. For in Thee I put my trust and hope, and to Thee, together with Thy eternal Father and the all-holy Spirit, I ascribe all praise, honor, and glory, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Prayer before a journey; cf. the Book of Needs (Trebnik), the Office for those setting forth on a journey

prayers.title: Before Beginning Any Task
prayers.body: Almighty God, our Help and Refuge, Fountain of wisdom and Tower of strength, Who knowest that I can do nothing without Thy guidance and help: assist me, I pray Thee, and direct me by Thy divine wisdom and power, that I may accomplish this task, and whatever I may undertake to do, faithfully and diligently, according to Thy will, so that it may be profitable to myself and others, and to the glory of Thy holy Name. For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.note: Prayed at the start of any work, study, or undertaking, asking God's blessing on its labor and outcome.
prayers.src: Prayer before undertaking any work, received in the Antiochian Orthodox prayer-book tradition

prayers.title: For Protection
prayers.body: Let God arise, and let His enemies be scattered; and let those who hate Him flee from before His face. As smoke vanishes, so let them vanish; as wax melts before the fire, so let the demons perish before the face of those who love God and who sign themselves with the Sign of the Cross, and who say with gladness: Rejoice, most precious and life-giving Cross of the Lord, for thou drivest away the demons by the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, Who was crucified upon thee, and descended into hell, and trampled down the power of the devil, and gave us thee, His precious Cross, for the driving away of every adversary. O most precious and life-giving Cross of the Lord, help me, together with the holy Lady Virgin Theotokos, and with all the saints, unto the ages. Amen.
prayers.note: The Prayer to the Precious Cross. May be prayed for oneself and for those one loves; Psalm 90 is also read for protection.
prayers.src: Orthodox Daily Prayers, St. Tikhon's Seminary Press (public domain)

prayers.title: For the Sick
prayers.body: O holy Father, heavenly Physician of our souls and bodies, Who hast sent Thine only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, to heal all our ailments and deliver us from death: do Thou visit and heal Thy servant (Name), granting him release from pain and restoration to health and vigor, that he may give thanks unto Thee and bless Thy holy Name, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.note: Insert the name of the sick person; say her, she, where fitting.
prayers.src: Intercessory prayer for the sick, Antiochian Orthodox prayer-book tradition; cf. the Book of Needs (Trebnik)

prayers.title: For Those in Authority
prayers.body: O Lord our God, by Whom kings reign and rulers govern: we beseech Thee, according to the word of Thine Apostle, to receive our supplications and prayers for all who are set in authority over us. Remember, O Lord, the civil authorities of our land, those who lead and serve in government, and all to whom Thou hast entrusted office and oversight. Speak peace and goodness into their hearts, grant them wisdom and the fear of God, and incline them to justice and mercy, that under their governance we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For Thou art our God, and unto Thee we ascribe glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.note: Following the Apostle's exhortation to pray for kings and all in authority (1 Timothy 2:1-2), and the daily commemoration of the civil authorities.
prayers.src: After 1 Timothy 2:1-2, with the daily intercession of the Church (Orthodox Daily Prayers, public domain)

prayers.title: For the Armed Forces
prayers.body: O Lord God of hosts, O God of our salvation, O God Who alone workest wonders: look down with mercy and compassion upon Thy humble servants, and out of love for mankind hearken and have mercy on us. Look with mercy, we pray Thee, O Lord, upon those of our sons and daughters who serve in the Armed Forces, and who, in obedience to those set over them, have for our sakes placed themselves in harm's way. Grant that those who seek the protection of Thy right hand may be overpowered by no adverse force, and may the defense of Thy mighty power shield Thy faithful servants. Watch over them, O Lord, and bring them back safe to those who love them. Grant courage and steadfast faith to them, and to those who long for their return. Bring a quick and bloodless end to all conflict, and spare the lives of the innocent. Grant no increase to the numbers of widows and orphans, and relieve the privations of the bereaved and the wounded, whether wounded in body or in soul. Restore peace in our day, O Lord; for Thou art the Prince of Peace, and art ever glorified with the Father and the all-holy and good and life-giving Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Prayer for the armed forces, received in the Antiochian Orthodox prayer-book tradition

prayers.title: For Priests and Clergy
prayers.body:
O Lord Jesus Christ, enkindle the hearts of all Thy priests with the fire of zealous love for Thee, that they may ever seek Thy glory. Give them strength, that they may labor unceasingly in Thine earthly vineyard for the salvation of our souls and the glory of Thine all-honorable and majestic Name, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Save, O Lord, and have mercy on our bishops, priests, and deacons, and on all the clergy whom Thou hast appointed to tend Thy reason-endowed flock; and through their prayers have mercy on me, a sinner, and save me.
prayers.src: Prayer for priests, with the daily commemoration of the clergy (Orthodox Daily Prayers, public domain)

prayers.title: For Peace
prayers.body: O Master, Lover of mankind, King of the ages and Giver of all good things: we thank Thee for breaking down the dividing wall of enmity and granting peace to those who seek Thy mercy. Awaken the longing for a peaceful life in all who are filled with hatred for their neighbors, and especially in those who make war or prepare for war. Grant peace to Thy servants; implant in them the fear of Thee, and confirm in them love one for another; extinguish every dispute, and banish all temptations to discord. Remember and have mercy on all who suffer from acts of war, and lead everyone along the path of reconciliation and peace. Grant, O Lord, peace, love, and a swift reconciliation to Thy people, whom Thou hast redeemed with Thy precious Blood; that all may praise Thine all-holy Name, O long-suffering Lord; for Thou art our peace, and unto Thee we ascribe glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: A prayer for peace of the Orthodox Church

prayers.title: For One's Community
prayers.body: O Lord our God, look down from Thy holy dwelling upon this community in which Thou hast set us to live. Save and have mercy on all who serve and labor in Thy holy Church, on those who govern and on those who are governed, on our neighbors near and far, on the aged and the young, the poor, the orphan and the widow, and on all who are in sickness, in sorrow, in want, or in any affliction. Surround them with peace, and speak peace and goodness into their hearts; that we may live together a calm and quiet life in true faith, in all godliness and purity, loving one another and bearing one another's burdens, to the glory of Thy holy Name, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.note: For one's parish, neighborhood, and city.
prayers.src: The daily intercession for the living (Orthodox Daily Prayers, public domain)

prayers.title: For Those Who Travel
prayers.body: O Lord Jesus Christ our God, the true and living way: be Thou the companion, guide, and guardian of Thy servants (names) who travel; deliver and protect them from all danger, misfortune, and temptation, that, defended by Thy divine power, they may have a peaceful journey and arrive safely at their destination. Restore them in health and safety to those who love them; for Thou art the Guardian of all, and unto Thee we ascribe glory, with Thine eternal Father and the all-holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.note: Insert the names of those traveling.
prayers.src: Intercessory prayer for travelers; cf. the Book of Needs (Trebnik), the Office for those setting forth on a journey

prayers.title: For Our Enemies
prayers.body:
O merciful Lord, by Thy Holy Spirit teach us to love our enemies, and to pray for them with tears. O Lord, send down Thy Holy Spirit upon the earth, that all peoples may know Thee, and learn Thy love.

O Lord, as Thou Thyself didst pray for Thine enemies, so teach us also, by Thy Holy Spirit, to love our enemies. O Lord, all peoples are the work of Thy hands; turn them from enmity and malice to repentance, that all may know Thy love.

O Lord, Thou didst command us to love our enemies, but it is hard for us sinners, if Thy grace be not with us. Pour down Thy grace upon the earth; let all the peoples of the earth come to know Thy love, and to know that Thou lovest us with a love greater than a mother's, and that Thy love for Thy creation is boundless. O merciful Lord, by the riches of Thy mercy, save all peoples. Amen.
prayers.src: St. Silouan the Athonite

prayers.title: For Those Suffering in Mind and Soul
prayers.body: Heavenly Father, Physician of our souls and bodies, Who didst send Thine only-begotten Son and our Lord Jesus Christ to heal every sickness and infirmity: visit and heal also Thy servants who are sick in soul and body; deliver them from all ailments of mind and spirit, from despondency, fear, and the darkening of thoughts; grant them rest, peace, and the return of hope. Strengthen those who care for them, and grant to physicians wisdom and to the suffering patience; through the prayers of our most holy Lady the Theotokos, and of all the saints, now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.note: An intercession for another. Because it asks the healing of the soul as well as the body, it is fitting for those who suffer in mind, in despondency, or in distress. Seek also the help of a priest and, where needed, of a physician.
prayers.src: Prayer for the sick of soul and body, Orthodox prayer book (received text)

prayers.title: For Doctors and Nurses
prayers.body:
O Lord Jesus Christ our God, Lover of Mankind, Physician of our souls and bodies, who didst bear the pain of our infirmities, and by whose wounds we are healed; Who gave sight to the man born blind; Who straightened the woman who was bent over for 18 years; Who gave speech and sight to the mute demoniac; Who not only forgave the paralytic his sins, but healed him to walk; Who restored the withered hand of a troubled man; Who stopped the flow of blood of her who bled for 12 years; Who raised Jairus' daughter to life; And brought the four-days-dead Lazarus to life; And who heals every infirmity under the sun:

Do now, O Lord, grant Thy grace to all those here gathered who have labored and studied hour upon hour, to go into all the world, and also to heal by the talent Thou hast given to each of them. Strengthen them, by Thy strength, to fear no evil or disease. Enlighten them to do no evil by the works of their hands, and preserve them and those they serve in peace, for Thou art our God, and we know no other, and to Thee we ascribe glory together with Thy Father who is from everlasting, and Thy most Holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.note: For physicians, nurses, and all who care for the sick.
prayers.src: Orthodox prayer for doctors and nurses (saintgregoryoutreach.org).

prayers.title: For Mental and Emotional Health
prayers.body: O my beloved Queen, my hope, O Mother of God, protector of orphans and defender of those who are hurt, the salvation of those who perish, and the consolation of all who are in distress: thou seest my misery, thou seest my sorrow and my loneliness. Help me, for I am powerless; give me strength. Thou knowest what I suffer; thou knowest my grief. Lend me thy hand, for who else can be my hope but thee, my protector and my intercessor before God? I have sinned before thee and before all people. Be thou my Mother, my consoler, my helper; protect me and save me; chase grief away from me; chase away my faintness of heart and my despondency. Help me, O Mother of my God. Amen.
prayers.note: A prayer in despondency, sorrow, or distress. It is no substitute for the care of a priest or, where needed, of a physician; the Church blesses the use of both.
prayers.src: Prayer to the Most Holy Theotokos in time of distress (received Russian Orthodox prayer; recorded in the life of Hieromartyr Arseny)

prayers.title: In Weariness and Exhaustion
prayers.body: O Thou Who at all times and at every hour, in heaven and on earth, art worshipped and glorified, O Christ God, long-suffering, plenteous in mercy and compassion, Who lovest the righteous and hast mercy on sinners, Who callest all to salvation through the promise of good things to come: receive, O Lord, our prayers at this hour, and direct our lives toward Thy commandments. Sanctify our souls, make chaste our bodies, correct our thoughts, purify our intentions, and deliver us from every sorrow, evil, and pain. Compass us about with Thy holy angels, that, guarded and guided by their host, we may attain to the unity of the faith and to the knowledge of Thine unapproachable glory; for blessed art Thou unto the ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.note: This prayer is appointed at each of the Hours through the day. Said in weariness or exhaustion, it lays the burden of the hour upon Christ, Who calleth the heavy-laden to come unto Him and find rest (Matthew 11:28).
prayers.src: The Prayer of the Hours, from the Horologion (received text), public domain

prayers.title: For a Right Measure and Humility
prayers.body: O Lord, I know not what to ask of Thee. Thou alone knowest what are my true needs. Thou lovest me more than I myself know how to love. O Father, grant unto me, Thy servant, what I myself know not how to ask. I dare not ask either a cross or a consolation; I can only wait upon Thee. My heart is open to Thee. Visit and help me, for Thy great mercy's sake. Strike me and heal me; cast me down and raise me up. I worship in silence Thy holy will and Thine inscrutable ways. I offer myself as a sacrifice unto Thee. I put all my trust in Thee. I have no other desire than to fulfill Thy will. Teach me how to pray; do Thou Thyself pray within me. Amen.
prayers.note: A prayer of surrender for those tempted to over-reach in the spiritual life. The right measure of prayer and fasting is given by God and confirmed by one's spiritual father; zeal without humility leads to despair when we fail and to vainglory when we succeed.
prayers.src: Morning Prayer of St. Philaret (Drozdov), Metropolitan of Moscow

prayers.title: For the Orthodox Departed
prayers.body:
O Christ, give rest to the souls of Thy servants with the saints, where there is no sickness, sorrow, or sighing, but life everlasting.

Remember, O Lord, the souls of Thy departed servants (names), and all who have fallen asleep in the hope of the Resurrection and life eternal. Forgive all their sins, both voluntary and involuntary. Grant them participation in Thine eternal good things, and the enjoyment of the eternal and blessed life.

Grant rest eternal in blessed repose, O Lord, to the souls of Thy departed servants, and make their memory to be eternal. Memory eternal! Memory eternal! Memory eternal!
prayers.note: Insert the name or names where indicated.
prayers.src: Orthodox Daily Prayers, St. Tikhon's Seminary Press (public domain)

prayers.title: For the Non-Orthodox Departed
prayers.body: Have mercy, O Lord, if it is possible, on the soul of Thy servant (Name), departed this life in separation from Thy Holy Orthodox Church. Unfathomable are Thy judgments. Do not account this prayer of mine as sin, but may Thy holy will be done.
prayers.note: A model for private prayer at home. The Church's liturgical commemoration of the departed is offered for the Orthodox faithful; this prayer, given by Elder Leo of Optina, is an example of how one may pray privately for those who reposed outside the Church.
prayers.src: Prayer of St. Leonid (Lev) of Optina for one departed outside the Orthodox Church

prayers.title: For One Who Has Taken His Own Life
prayers.body: Seek out, O Lord, the lost soul of Thy servant (Name); if it is possible, have mercy. Unfathomable are Thy judgments. Do not account this prayer of mine as sin, but may Thy holy will be done.
prayers.note: Composed by Elder Leo of Optina for a disciple grieving his father's death by suicide, and offered in private prayer at home. For anything beyond private prayer, consult your priest.
prayers.src: Prayer of St. Leonid (Lev) of Optina

prayers.title: To the Holy Martyr Varus (for the reposed outside the Church)
prayers.body:
O Holy, wondrous Martyr Varus, who, burning with zeal for the Heavenly King, didst confess Him before thy torturers and didst greatly suffer for Him! Now the Church doth venerate thee, as one glorified with the glory of heaven by Christ the Lord, Who granted thee the abundant grace to approach Him boldly.

And now, standing before Him together with the Angels, rejoicing on high, beholding the Most Holy Trinity clearly, and enjoying the Uncreated Light, remember the suffering of our relatives (and those we remember, and those we hold in our hearts) who have died outside the Faith, and accept our pleas; and as thou didst intercede for the unbelieving ancestors of Cleopatra and didst free them from eternal suffering, remember those who have died unbaptized, or have been buried in an ungodly manner, or died suddenly, or by their own hand, or unjustly (N.N.), and pray earnestly that they may be delivered from eternal darkness, that we may all, with one mouth and one heart, praise the Most Merciful Creator unto the ages of ages. Amen.

prayers.title: For Husband and Wife
prayers.body: O Merciful God, we beseech Thee ever to remind us that the married state is holy, and that we must keep it so. Grant us Thy grace, that we may continue in faithfulness and love. Increase in us the spirit of mutual understanding and trust, that no quarrel or strife may come between us. Grant us Thy blessings, that we may stand before our fellows and in Thy sight as an ideal family. And finally, by Thy mercy, account us worthy of everlasting life; for Thou art our sanctification, and to Thee we ascribe glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.
prayers.src: Prayer for husband and wife, received in the Antiochian Orthodox prayer-book tradition

prayers.title: For One's Children
prayers.body: O God, our heavenly Father, Who lovest mankind and art most merciful and compassionate, have mercy upon Thy servants (names), for whom I humbly pray Thee, and commend to Thy gracious care and protection. Be Thou, O God, their guide and guardian in all their endeavors; lead them in the path of Thy truth, and draw them nearer to Thee, that they may lead a godly and righteous life in Thy love and fear, doing Thy will in all things. Give them grace that they may be temperate, industrious, diligent, devout, and charitable. Defend them against the assaults of the enemy, and grant them wisdom and strength to resist all temptation and corruption of this life; and direct them in the way of salvation, through the merits of Thy Son, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and the intercessions of His most holy Mother and of all Thy blessed Saints. Amen.
prayers.note: Insert the name or names where indicated.
prayers.src: A parent's prayer for children, received in the Antiochian Orthodox prayer-book tradition

prayers.title: For One's Parents
prayers.body: O Lord and Savior, Thou hast taught us to honor our fathers and mothers, and to show love and obedience toward them. From the depth of my heart I fervently pray to Thee: hear my prayer, and bless my parents, who have raised me up with the help of Thy grace. Protect them from evil, harm, and sickness. Grant them faith, health, and joy, and bless all their works, that they may give Thee honor and glory all the days of their lives. Amen.
prayers.src: A prayer for one's parents, received in the Antiochian Orthodox prayer-book tradition

prayers.title: For Loved Ones
prayers.body:
Save, O Lord, and have mercy on my parents (names), my spouse (name), my children (names), my brothers and sisters, and all my kindred according to the flesh; on those who are close to my family, and on my friends. Grant them Thy good things, both earthly and heavenly.

Save, O Lord, and have mercy on those who hate and offend me, and do me harm, and do not let them perish because of me, a sinner. Enlighten with the light of Thy knowledge those who have gone astray, and reunite them to Thy Holy Church. By the multitude of Thy compassions, have mercy on all, and grant to all their every petition for salvation. Amen.
prayers.note: A prayer for the whole household, kindred, and friends. Insert names where indicated.
prayers.src: Orthodox Daily Prayers, St. Tikhon's Seminary Press (public domain)

prayers.title: Psalm 50 (51): Of Repentance
prayers.body:
Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy; and according to the multitude of Thy compassions blot out my transgression. Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I know mine iniquity, and my sin is ever before me. Against Thee only have I sinned, and done this evil in Thy sight, that Thou mightest be justified in Thy words, and prevail when Thou art judged.

For behold, I was conceived in iniquities, and in sins did my mother bear me. For behold, Thou hast loved truth; the hidden and secret things of Thy wisdom hast Thou made manifest unto me. Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be made clean; Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow. Thou shalt make me to hear joy and gladness; the bones that be humbled shall rejoice. Turn Thy face away from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities. Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me. Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation, and establish me with Thy governing Spirit.

I shall teach transgressors Thy ways, and the ungodly shall turn back unto Thee. Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, Thou God of my salvation; my tongue shall rejoice in Thy righteousness. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips, and my mouth shall declare Thy praise. For if Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I had given it; with whole-burnt offerings Thou shalt not be pleased. A sacrifice unto God is a broken spirit; a heart that is broken and humbled God will not despise. Do good, O Lord, in Thy good pleasure unto Zion, and let the walls of Jerusalem be builded. Then shalt Thou be pleased with a sacrifice of righteousness, with oblation and whole-burnt offerings. Then shall they offer bullocks upon Thine altar.
prayers.note: The Psalm of repentance, read daily at the Midnight Office and Matins, and in preparation for Confession. Psalm 51 in the Hebrew numbering.
prayers.src: The Psalter (Septuagint numbering)

prayers.title: Psalm 22 (23): The Lord Is My Shepherd
prayers.body:
The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: He leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: He leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for His name's sake.

Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff they comfort me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: Thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.
prayers.note: A psalm of trust and comfort, and a psalm of preparation for Holy Communion. Psalm 23 in the Hebrew numbering.
prayers.src: The Psalter (King James Version, public domain)

prayers.title: Psalm 90 (91): For Protection
prayers.body:
He that dwelleth in the secret place of the Most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in Him will I trust. Surely He shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence. He shall cover thee with His feathers, and under His wings shalt thou trust: His truth shall be thy shield and buckler.

Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday. A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee. Because thou hast made the Lord, which is my refuge, even the Most High, thy habitation; there shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling. For He shall give His angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.

Because he hath set his love upon Me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known My name. He shall call upon Me, and I will answer him: I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and honor him. With long life will I satisfy him, and show him My salvation.
prayers.note: The psalm of protection, read for deliverance from danger and at Compline. Psalm 91 in the Hebrew numbering.
prayers.src: The Psalter (King James Version, public domain)

prayers.title: Psalm 102 (103): Of Thanksgiving
prayers.body:
Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless His holy name. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; Who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; Who crowneth thee with loving-kindness and tender mercies; Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle's.

The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy. He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities. For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is His mercy toward them that fear Him. As far as the east is from the west, so far hath He removed our transgressions from us. Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear Him. For He knoweth our frame; He remembereth that we are dust.

Bless the Lord, ye His angels, that excel in strength, that do His commandments, hearkening unto the voice of His word. Bless ye the Lord, all His hosts; ye ministers of His, that do His pleasure. Bless the Lord, all His works in all places of His dominion: bless the Lord, O my soul.
prayers.note: A psalm of thanksgiving and blessing, sung at the Divine Liturgy. Psalm 103 in the Hebrew numbering.
prayers.src: The Psalter (King James Version, public domain)

prayers.title: To the Saint of the Day
prayers.body:
O heavenly hosts of holy Angels and Archangels, pray for us sinners.

O glorious Apostles, Prophets, Martyrs, and all Saints, pray for us sinners.

Pray to God for me, holy ____________, for with fervor I run to you, the swift helper and intercessor for my soul.
